title: Mitigating Write Disturbance in Non-Volatile Memory via Coupling Machine Learning with Out-of-Place Updates
problem: Write disturbance in NVM causes unintended cell value transformations that deteriorate memory reliability and access performance. This prevents practical deployment of NVM as main memory.
motivation: Non-volatile memory promises to resolve main memory scaling limitations, but write disturbance remains a critical barrier to deployment.
method: LearnWD uses clustering to group memory data based on how prone each piece is to errors. For each write operation, it evaluates how aggressively the new data would overwrite existing data and how vulnerable the existing data is to damage, then predicts which approach will minimize write disturbance errors. The system integrates with various memory encoding schemes (methods of protecting data against errors), allowing error-reduction efforts to combine cumulatively.
key_novelty: The innovation pairs machine learning classification of error-prone data with out-of-place updates (writing to fresh memory locations instead of overwriting), reducing write disturbance more than traditional in-place encoding approaches.
contributions: LearnWD framework combining machine learning with out-of-place updates for write disturbance mitigation
Clustering-based classification of stale data by error proneness
Speculative WD error minimization integrated with multiple encoding schemes
Demonstrated 20.1% WD error reduction, 11.0% write latency improvement, 21.9% write endurance extension across 15 real-world datasets

metrics.other: 20.1% WD error reduction, 21.9% write endurance extension

primary_theme: Machine learning for NVM write disturbance mitigation
